newsitem.title: USA: Cinergi to sell film library to Disney.
newsitem.headline: Cinergi to sell film library to Disney.

text.p: Cinergi Pictures Entertainment Inc said on Thursday it reached an agreement to sell substantially all of the films in Cinergi's motion picture library and certain other assets to Walt Disney Co.
In exchange, Disney has agreed to relinquish its equity interest in Cinergi and cancel about $38.4 million in outstanding loans to Cinergi.

In addition, Disney has agreed to assume with respect to the films and rights being sold to Disney, all residual obligations, as well as all scheduled obligations relating to Cinergi's existing exploitation agreements.
Cinergi said Disney has agreed to assume the outstanding debt under Cinergi's credit facility relating to the soon to be completed "An Alan Smithee Film."
Cinergi also said it has agreed to transfer to Disney all minimum guarantee payments and any overages paid or to be paid with respect to the film.

The film library being sold to Disney includes primarily all of Cinergi's rights to 11 films, including "Medicine Man", "Tombstone", "Renaissance Man", "Color of Night", "Judge Dredd", "The Scarlet Letter", "Nixon", "Evita", "The Shadow Conspiracy" and "An Alan Smithee Film".
Disney will also retain overages otherwise payable to Cinergi by Disney with respect to certain distribution rights to "Die Hard, With a Vengeance" previously licensed to Disney.
In addition, upon completion of the sale to Disney, Cinergi's 25 film domestic distribution arrangement with an affiliate of Disney, under which nine films have been delivered, will be terminated.
The agreement and related sale of assets may also be terminated by Cinergi or Disney in certain circumstances, including the failure to consummate the sale by September 15, 1997.

Cinergi said management, including Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Andrew Vajna, which owns approximately 43.7 percent of the outstanding common stock of Cinergi, has agreed to vote its shares in favour of the transaction in accordance with the terms of the agreement with Disney.

Separately, Cinergi said it does not intend to begin production on any additional motion pictures and it is in the process of considering its alternatives assuming consummation of the library sale to Disney.
Such alternatives include disposing of those assets which are not being sold to Disney, in one or a series of transactions, the company said.

Not included in the sale to Disney are Cinergi's slate of approximately 40 development projects, Cinergi's visual effects facility, and Cinergi's rights in "Die Hard, With a Vengeance" which Cinergi owns with News Corp's Twentieth Century Fox, which controls the sequel rights to the film.
Also not included in the sale to Disney are any rights with respect to the film "Broadway Brawler" on which production ceased after the start of principal photography.

Cinergi said it is currently in discussions with certain parties involved in the production of "Broadway Brawler" regarding settlement of various obligations. Cinergi said it expects no significant amounts will be outstanding under its credit facility after payment of the debt relating to "Broadway Brawler" and assumption by Disney, in accordance with the agreement announced, of the debt relating to "An Alan Smithee Film".

Cinergi said any decision made regarding its alternatives assuming consummation of the film library sale to Disney, will effectively result, after provision for Cinergi's remaining liabilities, in a cash payment to Cinergi's stockholders in exchange for their equity interests in Cinergi.
